## Why this unit matters

Replace a synchronous confirmation side effect with an order.placed event. Learn binders, consumers, groups, partitions, duplicates and delivery guarantees.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Spring Cloud Stream: Core Concepts](stream-abstractions.qmd)**
2. **[Stream Producers and Consumers](stream-producers-consumers.qmd)**
3. **[Consumer Groups and Partitions](stream-groups-partitions.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Mathematical Abstraction

Event-based coupling introduces a producer-to-consumer dependency through a broker.

$$
\mathrm{Order}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{publish}}B\xrightarrow{\mathrm{deliver}}\mathrm{Consumer}
$$

$B$ represents a broker. Publication, delivery and processing completion are separate events with distinct failure windows.
